summary: wazuh.manager (Amazon Linux 2023) scores 52% on the CIS benchmark cis_amazon_linux_2023 with 46 failed checks. The most important issues are: no host firewall (nftables) in front of the Wazuh enrollment, agent and API ports that listen on all interfaces; weak local password handling; no auditd, so most audit-rule checks fail; and a world-writable /usr/bin/sh seen by FIM. Most other failures are permission and hygiene checks that can be fixed in one pass.

fixes.title: Install and enforce a default-deny host firewall in front of ports 1514, 1515 and 55000
fixes.why: Agent enrollment (1515), agent events (1514) and the Wazuh API (55000, on both 0.0.0.0 and ::) listen on all interfaces. nftables is not installed and no table, base chains or default-drop policy exist, so nothing on the host restricts who can reach these services. Enrollment and API access are authentication-sensitive. Note that the listening-ports data shows no process names, so the services behind them are inferred, not confirmed. If this host runs in a container, also check the container or cloud-level network rules.
fixes.remediation: dnf install nftables; nft create table inet filter; nft create chain inet filter input { type filter hook input priority 0 \; }; nft create chain inet filter forward { type filter hook forward priority 0 \; }; nft create chain inet filter output { type filter hook output priority 0 \; }. Before setting the drop policy, add accept rules for established connections, loopback, SSH from admin addresses if used, and tcp 1514/1515/55000 from known agent and admin source ranges only. Then set: nft chain inet filter input { policy drop \; } and the same for forward. Test from a second session because changing firewall rules over the network can lock you out.

fixes.title: Fix password storage and password aging policy
fixes.why: Accounts in /etc/passwd are not all using shadowed passwords, meaning password hashes may be readable by any local user (the file must stay world-readable). Hashing is not confirmed as SHA-512, and aging settings (maximum age, minimum age, inactivity lock) are not met. These weaken resistance to offline cracking and brute force.
fixes.remediation: Run: sed -e 's/^\([a-zA-Z0-9_]*\):[^:]*:/\1:x:/' -i /etc/passwd (first investigate any account that held a hash in /etc/passwd and reset its password). In /etc/login.defs set ENCRYPT_METHOD SHA512, PASS_MAX_DAYS 365, PASS_MIN_DAYS 7. In /etc/libuser.conf set crypt_style = sha512. Configure pam_unix.so for sha512 in the authselect custom system-auth and password-auth files. Run useradd -D -f 30, then apply to existing users: chage --maxdays 365 --mindays 7 --inactive 30 <user>.

fixes.title: Correct the world-writable /usr/bin/sh and lock down sshd_config permissions
fixes.why: FIM reports /usr/bin/sh with mode rwxrwxrwx, owned by root. If this is a real file or a link whose target is writable, any local user could replace the system shell, which is a direct privilege escalation path. It may just be a symlink (symlinks normally show as rwxrwxrwx), so verify before acting. Separately, /etc/ssh/sshd_config fails its ownership/permission check, which allows non-root modification of SSH settings.
fixes.remediation: Run ls -l /usr/bin/sh and readlink -f /usr/bin/sh. If it is a symlink to /usr/bin/bash, check that the target is root:root with mode 755 (chmod 755 /usr/bin/bash). If it is a regular file, restore it with: dnf reinstall bash and compare with rpm -V bash. Then run: chown root:root /etc/ssh/sshd_config; chmod og-rwx /etc/ssh/sshd_config.
evidence: FIM: /usr/bin/sh perm rwxrwxrwx owner root, mtime 2026-10-16T10:47:59

fixes.title: Install auditd and load the CIS audit rules, then make them immutable
fixes.why: auditd is not installed, so none of the audit rule checks can pass and there is no kernel-level record of privilege use, identity file changes, logins, module loading or time changes. Audit configuration is not immutable, and local logging pieces (rsyslog, journal remote, time sync) are also missing, so an attacker with root could erase the trail and timestamps would be unreliable. This is a large share of the 46 failures and is resolved mostly by one package plus rule files.
fixes.remediation: dnf install audit rsyslog chrony systemd-journal-remote; systemctl enable --now auditd rsyslog chronyd. Create rule files in /etc/audit/rules.d/ for: sudoers (-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k scope, -w /etc/sudoers.d -p wa -k scope), user emulation, time-change, system-locale, identity (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group, /etc/gshadow, /etc/security/opasswd), mounts, session (utmp/wtmp/btmp), logins (lastlog, faillock), deletes, MAC-policy, chcon, setfacl, chacl, usermod and kernel modules. Add -e 2 last in /etc/audit/rules.d/99-finalize.rules, then run augenrules --load (a reboot is needed for immutable mode). Set log_group = adm in /etc/audit/auditd.conf and run chgrp adm /var/log/audit/ and chgrp adm on files in it. Use the exact rule text from each check's remediation.

fixes.title: Batch-fix scheduler, boot, package-trust and banner hygiene
fixes.why: Cron, at and bootloader files are not restricted to root, which can enable local privilege escalation through scheduled jobs and exposure of boot parameters. gpgcheck is not globally enabled, so unsigned packages could be installed. AIDE and sudo are not installed, and an unneeded FTP server package (vsftpd) is present, which increases attack surface. Login banners expose OS details. These are low-effort local hygiene fixes.
fixes.remediation: chown root:root /etc/crontab /etc/cron.hourly /etc/cron.daily /etc/cron.weekly /etc/cron.monthly /etc/cron.d; chmod og-rwx on each. Restrict cron and at: rm -f /etc/cron.deny /etc/at.deny; touch /etc/cron.allow /etc/at.allow; chown root:root both; chmod u-x,go-rwx both. Bootloader: chown root:root /boot/grub2/grub.cfg /boot/grub2/grubenv; chmod og-rwx /boot/grub2/grub.cfg; chmod u-x,og-rwx /boot/grub2/grubenv (and user.cfg if present). Set gpgcheck=1 in /etc/dnf/dnf.conf and every file in /etc/yum.repos.d/. Run dnf remove vsftpd; dnf install sudo aide; aide --init && mv /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new.gz /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz. Set /etc/issue and /etc/issue.net to a policy text without \m \r \s \v.

coverage.note: This brief is based on 46 failed SCA checks from cis_amazon_linux_2023 (score 52), 20 recent FIM entries out of 1100 total, and the listening-port list. Known limits: FIM data is a baseline only, with no change since first indexing, so it shows no evidence of tampering but cannot confirm integrity (this includes the /usr/bin/sh finding). Alerts and vulnerability detection were not available because the service reads only the server API and not the indexer, so exploitable software flaws and active attacks were not assessed. Listening ports show no process names, and the input has no firewall rules or container/network-level controls, so actual exposure may differ.
gaps: File integrity data is a baseline only: none of the most recently modified files has changed since FIM first indexed it.
Alerts and vulnerability detection are not included: the service reads the server API only, not the indexer.
